$comment: The id a node that its run prices from a server-side measure (or not at all before the run) is QUOTED at, on BOTH estimates over the same node: the editor's (frontend getModelIdentifier — the node's pill, its Run button, the confirm and the workflow badge) and the server's run estimate (CreditsService.estimateWorkflowCreditsAt — also the credit check before a run and an app's listing), which used to name the bare node type (priced nowhere: 0). Cinematic Avatar: the exact (resolution, duration) id its run holds, Auto at the 15 s ceiling, a duration clamped to 4–15 s (resolveCinematicCreditId). SwitchX: the 240-frame worst-case tier at the node's frame size, the most a run holds and what a workflow run holds (switchXQuoteCreditId: maxResolution 720 only for the number 720) — never a frame count the node's data carries. AI Avatar with no audio wired: the script's bucket in text mode, else the 120 s default (aiAvatarQuoteCreditId). `expected` is the credit id; the server's line is that id's price, above 0. Held by frontend/src/lib/__tests__/probed-node-quote-parity.test.ts and backend/src/ee/billing/__tests__/probed-node-quote-parity.test.ts.

cases.name: 1c. Cinematic Avatar on Auto: the 15 s ceiling (the length is the model's, known only after the run)
1d. Cinematic Avatar with a duration past its range (an API write): clamped to 15 s, as the run holds it
1e. Cinematic Avatar with no settings: its defaults
2. SwitchX at its default 1080p: the 240-frame worst-case tier
2c. SwitchX whose data carries a frame count (a client's word): still the worst-case tier
2d. SwitchX with maxResolution written as text (an API write): 1080p, as a workflow run holds it
3. AI Avatar in audio mode with nothing wired: the 120 s default, a minimum
3b. AI Avatar in text mode: its script's bucket (600 characters, about 50 s)
3c. AI Avatar whose data carries a probed length (a client's word): never read
